## U17 closeout — reload absence and results navigation (9 October 2026)

- **Authorisation (research owner, 9 October 2026; recorded before the
  first source edit).** An exceptional closeout beyond U17's two
  correction rounds, limited to: (1) the approved ruling on a reload
  before the desk was opened (below); (2) the approved correction of
  CLOSE HELP on the results view (the existing 400 ms fresh-press /
  settle discipline applied to that transition, so a carried second
  pointer or keyboard press never activates NEXT / BACK, never switches
  the displayed packet and never creates its `results_shown` record; a
  deliberate later navigation remains possible); (3) one focused,
  instrumented reproduction of the failing episode-1 route for the M05
  timing (diagnostic only: the route, the M05 rules, the cap and the
  production telemetry unchanged; no faked time, no injected
  measurement state, no weakened assertion); (4) the documentation
  dispositions — the separate exposure fields and `never_opened_reason`
  accepted as satisfying the intended distinction between briefing,
  opening and answering; the lure tests retained as logical consistency
  checks, never claimed to reproduce participants' actual misreadings or
  to establish empirical validity; the minor typography points and the
  non-Windows font checks carried into U24 / release verification; the
  two previously reproduced baseline test failures retained as
  documented exceptions; (5) verification — the complete M14 pure suite
  with the new reload-classification and results / help transition
  cases; the affected real-browser scenarios (a genuine reload before
  the desk was opened; pointer and keyboard double-press protection when
  leaving help on the results; the prior-opening hold-back kept for an
  orientation-only and a completed prior administration); the single
  instrumented episode-1 reproduction; typecheck, build, targeted lint
  and format checks, whitespace and verify-unit against the entry
  commit; (6) exactly one additional local commit
  `fix(m14): clarify reload absence and guard results navigation`,
  with 5d95e6e not amended, only after the checks pass, the review
  confirms the material fixes and the diagnostic is reported honestly.
  The existing 18-path allowlist is the maximum. Nothing else is
  authorised: no push, merge, PR, deployment, installation, worktree
  deletion or U18 work. Authored content, answer keys, the scoring
  formula, the 400 ms threshold and the canonical schema remain
  unchanged. Routing: Fable is the sole writer; Sonnet 5.5 runs the
  focused checks and analyses the timing evidence; one focused parallel
  Opus 5.5 scientific / gameplay review of the changed behaviour and the
  diagnostic conclusion; one bounded correction pass after the review,
  then the affected checks again and confirmation of the material fixes.
- **The approved ruling (reload before the desk was opened).** When the
  absence of a prior M14 opening is established, a page reload alone
  must not classify a subsequently available, never-opened desk as
  `interrupted`: before the briefing `not_presented`; briefed, never
  opened, the opportunity still open ⇒ null `pending` with
  `briefed_not_opened`; briefed, never opened, closed at the review ⇒
  null `no_eligible_event` with `briefed_not_opened`, censored,
  `closed_at_review`. An actual prior opening keeps the existing
  hold-back and `interrupted` classification — an orientation-only
  opening and a completed series included. A current-load briefing must
  not erase the evidence of an earlier opening; missing historical
  evidence must not be treated as proof of no prior exposure. The
  existing evidence that establishes these cases is identified first;
  the distinction is implemented inside the M14-specific code and the
  allowlist; the shared measurement framework and other items' reload
  policies are not changed; immutable earlier events, current-load
  extraction and the existing integrity checks are preserved. If the
  available evidence cannot establish the distinction, the independent
  work is finished and the precise limitation reported, never guessed.
- **Acceptance criteria.** (a) The pure suite passes with the new
  cases: absence established ⇒ `not_presented` / `pending` /
  `no_eligible_event` as ruled; absence not established (no check record
  of the load, a discontinuous history, a prior opening found) ⇒
  `interrupted`; the hold-back with a current-load briefing ⇒
  `interrupted` with the briefing read; CLOSE HELP on the results
  re-arms the 400 ms settle so a press inside it changes nothing and
  writes no `results_shown`, while a settled press navigates. (b) The
  browser: after a genuine reload before the opening the desk opens
  normally and the row reads the ruled dispositions; the doubled pointer
  and keyboard presses after CLOSE HELP on the results change nothing;
  R5 still shows the hold-back after an actual prior opening. (c) The
  diagnostic separates measured findings from inference and states
  whether the trace explains the missing start event, whether M14
  behaves correctly with respect to the M05 clock, and whether the
  failure is a scripted-route timing limitation or an identified U17
  regression; no "pre-existing" label without comparable evidence. (d)
  Typecheck, build, lint, format, whitespace and verify-unit clean
  against 5d95e6e. (e) The review confirms the material fixes; one
  commit; the handoff.

### U17 closeout results (9 October 2026)

- **Evidence identified first (ruling (a)).** The extractor reads the
  current page load's raw events only (`pilotCoverage.ts` passes
  `eventLogger.getEvents()`; `ExtractContext` carries `pageLoadIndex`
  and `reloaded` and no earlier events); the kit's `presented` record
  carries fixed fields; no model event precedes an opening — so no
  existing current-load record could establish the absence of an
  earlier opening, and every reloaded load without an opening read
  `interrupted`. The evidence that CAN establish it is the runtime's
  recovered history (`getPriorPageLoadEvents()`, the list the hold-back
  guard already reads) with its losslessness block (`getEventIntegrity()`:
  contiguous sequence numbers from 1, no duplicate, the meta record
  readable). The guard now writes that finding once per later load as
  the provisional record `prior_load_checked` at Concourse entry; the
  extractor reads the ruled dispositions from it. Register §5.290 (a),
  §4 "Unit 17 closeout" (1).
- **Before / after examples (extractor rows, the same current-load
  evidence).** (1) Reload, Concourse entered, no briefing yet: before —
  `interrupted` ("no current-load desk evidence after a reload"); after —
  `not_presented` with `reload_check.prior_opening_absence_established:
  true` (and `prior_briefing_found: true` when the earlier load was
  briefed). (2) Reload, briefed in the new load, never opened, still
  open: before — `interrupted`; after — `pending`, `missing_reason`
  `briefed_not_opened`, `exposure.never_opened_reason` `briefed_not_opened`.
  (3) The same, closed at the review: before — `interrupted`; after —
  `no_eligible_event`, `briefed_not_opened`, censored, `closed_at_review`.
  (4) Reload at the opening screen, the Concourse never reached: before
  and after — `interrupted` (no check; the desk was never available in
  that load). (5) Reload after an actual earlier opening (orientation
  only, one answer, or all six): before and after — `interrupted`
  (`held_back_after_reload: true`, now beside `reload_check.
  prior_opening_found: true`); a briefing in the new load is read and
  erases nothing. (6) A history recovered with a gap, a duplicate, from
  chunks alone, or empty: `interrupted` ("the absence of an earlier
  opening not established"). (7) A presented record without a usable
  sequence, or a check of another opportunity: `technical_failure` on
  the established path exactly as on a first load (review F1).
- **Help-navigation evidence (ruling (b)).** Pure: on the results after
  six answers, HELP then CLOSE HELP, a NEXT press 100 ms later refused
  (keyboard and pointer), `results_shown` still 1, the packet unchanged;
  a NEXT press 400 ms later shows packet 2 and writes its one
  `results_shown`; the same for BACK on packet 2; the decision-view
  close of help leaves `results_shown_at_ms` null. Browser R9: ENTER
  ENTER on CLOSE HELP — packet 1 still shown, NEXT focused,
  `results_shown` 1 (frame c02); a settled ENTER — packet 2,
  `results_shown` 2; HELP by click, a double click on CLOSE HELP —
  packet 2 still shown, BACK focused, `results_shown` 2 (frame c03); a
  settled click on BACK — packet 1; `help_consulted` 2; the row
  `observed` 6 / 6.
- **The measured M05 timeline and conclusion (ruling (d)).** Register §4
  "Unit 17 closeout" (3) carries the full timeline; in short: eligible at
  0 s; surfaces open 6.1–8.1 s (plan board), 18.5–21.8 s (desk),
  29.3–31.3 s (quality packet), all excluded (`unusable_controls`
  7 318 ms against 7 373 ms measured); the gauge step 31.3–58.1 s
  counted; the cap at 67.3 s wall = 60 012 ms focused, 9.3 s into the
  walk toward the lamp and 8.7 s before the lamp opened; START on the
  lamp ⇒ `late_start` (`since_closure_ms` 9 165), `work_completed`
  (`late: true`), `started` never written. Conclusion: the trace explains
  the missing event; M14 behaves correctly with respect to the clock;
  the failure is a limitation of the scripted route's expectation (its
  cumulative focused time before the lamp exceeds the cap; a participant
  following Vale's briefed order faces the same cap), the desk step
  contributing about 10.4 s gross and no single step decisive; not an

**2.2 RESEARCH-OWNER DECISION D-U18-1 — APPROVED 10 October 2026**

The approval is for the provisional U18 / M15 implementation. The items below are recorded as they were put to the owner — the proposal, the recommendation, the consequence and the alternatives considered — with the selections marked. Rules of this contract that implement an item are tagged [O-n]. Record the ruling in the register (Unit 18 record and §5.291 onward) as an owner ruling with this date, not as an implementer default; it is not to be reopened.

1. [O-1] Content. The two boxes, the four wiring options per box, the four questions with three options each, the keys and the results lines of `U18-STIMULUS-PREVIEW.md` r5 §3–§5 are the administered content (`m15-s1-v1`, `m15-s2-v1`); their logical correctness does not establish empirical validity. "Unseen" is operationalised as in preview §7.3: a question's situation is never an exploration act, and its step trace equals no test listing and no test listing with its first step removed; sign-mirrored or partial listings are NOT excluded, because each answer must be inferable from the tests (S2-Q1's trace is the sign-mirror, and S1-Q2's a part, of a listing — preview §4.5, §5.5). Recommendation: approve. Consequence: the keys are fixed (S1-Q1 C "W does not move", S1-Q2 B "Q goes down", S2-Q1 B "Z goes down", S2-Q2 C "Z does not move"; wirings box 1 B, box 2 D); blind-choice chance is 1/3 per question.
   - Among the four OFFERED wirings, treated as equally plausible, each dial's test is needed for a prediction: S1-Q1 needs both tests, S2-Q1 needs TEST S, S2-Q2 needs TEST T, and S1-Q2 needs either test (preview §7.4). The r3 amendment replaced box 1 option C and box 2 option A to achieve this; the r4 amendment rewrote all six wrong options as four parallel four-link sentences of 47 characters, so the key is no longer the simplest option, with the same test dependence.
   - Remaining cues, disclosed and never read as proof of testing or understanding (preview §7.5):
     - box 1 (r5, with the selected A): one single-step surface rule picks the key and gives both box-1 keys with no test — link-substitution neighbours (B is the only option one substituted link from two others). Option A is the odd one out (two links no other option has), so "set A aside, then prefer dial symmetry" also picks B. Greatest per-dial reach and dial symmetry tie A and B. Recurrence rules rank B, C and D level. In this format A must carry a unique link to keep S1-Q2 open before testing (preview §4.3, §7.5);
     - box 2: no single option is singled out (exact crossing; ties on unique links, recurrence, connectivity, symmetry and neighbours), but per-dial reach and same-verb split the options A/D vs B/C and fix S2-Q2 without TEST T, and A is the single-verb option;
     - across both boxes, with no test (expected keys out of 4, for a participant following that one rule and picking uniformly among its choices): "drop the single-verb option, then prefer the greatest reach" 3; "pick the option closest to the others" 3; reach alone 2.5. That r5 improves on r3 (whose simplicity cue gave 3.5) rests partly on simplicity being the more natural preference — a judgement, not a measured fact;
     - SELECTED by the owner: box 1 A = `F raises W. G raises W. P raises Q. W lowers P.` (in place of r4's `F raises W. G raises W. P raises Q. P raises W.`); it drives every unit and uses both verbs, so reach ties A and B and the cross-box rule no longer singles out box 1's key, while the neighbour rule and the symmetry chain still pick B;
     - the question kind predicts every key ("BOOST present → goes down; otherwise → does not move" matches 4 of 4; the intuitive "lock stops, boost raises" matches 2);
     - three of four box-1 options imply S1-Q2's key.
   - Within this item the owner also chose for S2-Q1 — SELECTED: (a). The options were (a) as proposed, "what does unit Z do?" — recommended: the intuitive rule stays at 2 of 4, the question keeps its two-link sign composition, and "goes up" is never a key; or (b) "what does unit Y do?" (key A "Y goes up", results line in preview §7.5; checked with the saved `derivation/verify-alt-s2q1-askY.mjs`): the best kind rule falls to 3 of 4, the intuitive rule rises to 3 of 4, the inference becomes single-link, and "goes up" becomes the key once. Choosing (b) is an amendment (content and hashes change).

   Alternative to the whole item: ask the preparation to revise the content (e.g. other qualifying designs of `derivation/search-designs.all.txt`, or four-option combined questions with chance 1/4 and a heavier reading load) — the unit then waits.
2. [O-2] Exploration. TEST turns one dial up one notch from rest and lists the steps; unlimited, deterministic; the latest listing per dial stays on the bench through the box's questions; tests close when the box's wiring is recorded; LOCK, BOOST and joint turns are never available as tests. Recommendation: approve. Consequence: the exploration companion describes testing before the model commitment only, and no question's situation is ever displayed (item 1's definition). Alternative: tests stay open during the questions (lower memory demand, but exploration after the model blurs explore → commit → predict; the questions would still be unseen).
3. [O-3] Model commitment. Per box one of the four listed wirings or CANNOT TELL, confirmed and immutable, required before that box's questions are presented; the recorded wiring (or "CANNOT TELL") is shown during the questions; model correctness = the recorded wiring is the station wiring (CANNOT TELL is not correct), a companion only; whether each answer agrees with the answer the recorded wiring implies is reported as a component (`consistent_with_recorded_wiring`), null when the wiring was CANNOT TELL, the response is CANNOT SOLVE, or the recorded wiring's answer is magnitude-dependent under the analysis conventions of preview §7.2 (none of the eight options is, so the null case is a guard). Recommendation: approve. Consequence: model and prediction correctness are separable (four of the six wrong wirings imply the key of at least one question — preview §7.1). Alternative: free link drawing as in the v2 board (richer model data, a heavier interface and reading load, a new layout); or no CANNOT TELL (forces a guess into the model record).
4. [O-4] Feedback timing. Identical neutral acknowledgements; no correctness information about any wiring or answer until all four first predictions are recorded; then results for both boxes (recorded and station wiring, recorded and station answers, the approved results lines). Recommendation: approve. Consequence: no key can be learned between box 1 and box 2. Alternative: results after each box (box 1's explanations of LOCK and BOOST would inform box 2's first predictions).

Kai's laboratory briefing, which names the evidence table, records the M15 briefing exposure at its acknowledgement (the kit's `present`) — exposure only, never a bench opening or a question presentation. Before the briefing: `not_presented`. Briefed, never opened, the opportunity open: null `pending`, `missing_reason` `briefed_not_opened`. Briefed, never opened, at the review closure: null `no_eligible_event`, `briefed_not_opened`, censored, `closed_at_review`. `declined` never occurs (the bench offers no refusal). Recommendation: approve. Alternative: the general dispositions without the briefing distinction.
6. [O-6] Reload (the M14 closeout ruling §5.290 (a) applied to M15). The existing hold-back stays: an opening of this administration in an earlier page load of the session identity ⇒ the bench is never re-run in the new load (neutral closed record; prior exposure recorded; the load's row `interrupted`; the earlier events immutable). In addition, at the first Diagnostics Laboratory entry of a later page load the adapter writes the provisional record `prior_load_checked` (the §5.290 (a) fields); when it establishes the absence of an earlier opening with continuous history, the load is read exactly as a first load. Recommendation: approve. Consequence: a never-opened bench after a reload is not misread as interrupted; one more record and its integrity rules. Alternative: the general rule only — every reloaded load without M15 evidence is `interrupted`.

7. [O-7] Order, form and orientation. Fixed box order 1 → 2; within a box exploration and wiring, then question 1, then question 2; fixed wiring, question and option order; one form, no counterbalancing; an orientation card (preview §3.1) at the first opening with one worked reading example and no practice question or practice box. Recommendation: approve (the M14 ruling D-U17-1 item 3 is only precedent here). Consequence: box content and position are confounded and box 1 carries first contact with the bench; interface learning on box 1 is not separated from box 1's answers. Alternative: a short unscored practice box before box 1 (cleaner first contact, longer administration, more reading, new content to author and approve), or counterbalanced box order (needs a second form of assignment and an analysis of order effects at a small n).
8. [O-8] Partial evidence while the opportunity is open. One to three first predictions recorded and the series not yet closed (the participant still able to return before the Utility Deck review) ⇒ the row is null `pending`, the recorded answers kept in the components; at the review closure it becomes `incomplete` with the value and its observed denominator (your instruction of 9 October 2026: "partial accuracy retains its observed denominator and incomplete disposition"). A session that ends before the review (abandonment, a closed tab) therefore exports `pending` with the answers in the components, not an `incomplete` value. Recommendation: approve (the M13 / M14 convention; a value is not final while further answers can still be given). Alternative: export `incomplete` with the value whenever at least one answer exists, also while the series is open (a value that can still change in a later export of the same session).

The commitment mechanics of §3.4 (fresh press, settle), the leaving rules of §3.7 and the names of §9 apply existing approved rules and precedent and are ordinary engineering; they are listed as defaults in §17, not as decision items.

6. [A] A first response (and a recorded wiring) is written once and is immutable: no later act, reopening, results view, reload or closure changes or duplicates it.
7. [O-4] Neutral acknowledgement, IDENTICAL for every response whatever its kind or correctness: `Answer recorded for question N.` with NEXT QUESTION / NEXT BOX / SHOW RESULTS; same line, control, timing, layout. Nothing in the first-response phase reveals correctness (no colour, glyph, sound, counter or wording that differs with correctness); the status may count answers recorded (`N of 4 answers recorded.`), never correct ones.
8. [P][D-4] Settle on EVERY view transition (§5.290 (b) generalised as the M14 closeout applied it): a press that arrives within 400 ms after a view appeared — the orientation's START, a box's first view, a question's first view, an acknowledgement, the results views (NEXT BOX / BACK / FINISH), the help sheet and the view restored by CLOSE HELP — changes nothing (no draft, no navigation, no commit request, no `results_shown`). CLOSE HELP re-arms the settle of the view it restores. So no carried press — the second ENTER, the second click of a double click, a repeated key — can draft, request, confirm, navigate or close in a newly opened view.

**3.5 Results [O-4]**
- Only when all four first predictions are recorded; a partial or review-closed series never shows results. SHOW RESULTS opens one view per box (preview §3.6; BACK / NEXT BOX / FINISH). Reopening a completed bench shows the results again, read-only; only the first showing of each box's results is recorded (`results_shown`).

**3.6 Help [D-5]**
HELP (H or the button) at any time except while a confirmation is open; the preview §3.5 sheet; informational; every consult recorded with the box, step and question it was opened on.

**3.7 Leaving, closure, reload, faults**
- [P] ESC closes, in order, an open dialog, then the help sheet, then leaves; LEAVE BENCH leaves; both take the SAME path (window pause, clock pause, surface close — the M14 host precedent `m14SurfaceHost`). Leaving keeps everything (box, step, test record, draft, recorded wiring, answers); returning never presents a question again and never starts a new trial. There is no STOP control.
- [P] Station-record closure at the Utility Deck review (`reviewClosure.ts` → `closeM15AtReview`): a series in its first-response phase (orientation, exploration, wiring or questions) closes as `closed_at_review` (system): recorded answers and wirings kept, unanswered questions missing; no results afterwards; the bench then opens as the closed record of preview §3.7 showing `N of 4 answers recorded.`. A completed series is not reclosed. A never-opened bench is recorded absent with the kit's `markAbsent` (`briefed_not_opened` / `not_briefed_not_opened`).
- [O-6][P] Reload: the hold-back of §2.2 item 6 (detail beginning `reload`), the closed record of preview §3.7, prior exposure recorded, the series marked technically incomplete; the earlier events immutable in `prior_page_load_events`; also when the earlier load completed all four. `prior_load_checked` once per later page load, at the first `guardM15Reload` run (Diagnostics Laboratory `create()`), before the hold-back record when an opening is found. A bench never opened before the reload runs normally.
- A fault while the first-response phase is open closes the series as a technical failure through the window kit and leaves the laboratory usable; a dialog never stays stuck after a cancelled callback.

**3.8 Wording and presentation limits**
Forbidden in every participant-facing string of the bench (tested by pattern, case-insensitive): `proto_`, `secondary_`, `M##`, `Q##`, score, trait, puzzle, persist, grit, skill, ability, intelligen, information, complex, "make sense", handle; "solve" only inside "CANNOT SOLVE". Before the fourth first prediction no correctness word (correct, incorrect, right, wrong, station answer, station wiring). The orientation and the help sheet name no dial or unit of either box (their examples use J, K, M, N), so they state no link of the instrument. Beyond the pattern (review criterion): no praise, blame or judgement. Pointer and keyboard each reach every control. Layout envelope (mockup evidence `layout-evidence\`): 16 px design text, 20 px title; wiring options as one-line tiles in the bench column (never in the 300 px column); one-line footer; at least 30 design px between the lowest control and the feedback line's top under the default font and under forced Courier New and Lucida Console; never smaller text, clipped or shortened wording, scrolling, or a larger minimum window.

**7 Success behaviour**

On the ordinary route (routeToLabWork, Kai's briefing) the evidence table presents the orientation, then box 1 and box 2 in order; in each box the dials can be tested as often as wanted, one wiring (or CANNOT TELL) is recorded once and closes the tests, then each question is presented after the previous first response and takes exactly one immutable first response, answered only by the identical neutral acknowledgement; no correctness information appears before the fourth answer; then the results follow without touching any response; leaving and returning resume the same state; the export carries `m15_correct_first_predictions` with value = numerator = questions whose first response is the keyed option, denominator = questions with a first response, planned denominator 4, the by-box split, model correctness and exploration in the components, and the dispositions of §10 — complete and stable from the fourth first response — reproducible from the raw events alone; the cipher writes only its secondary identity and never reaches the M15 row; every check of §12 was run and reported with its true result; the reviews of §15 are closed; one local commit exists (§16).

**8 Failure and recovery behaviour**

Never opened (before / after the briefing), opened at the orientation only, opened with tests but no wiring, opened with one to three answers, closed at the review with or without answers, held back after a reload, technically failed and completed are distinct records (§10). A double press, a doubled confirmation, a carried press into a new view, a re-entry or a resumed surface never duplicates a presentation, a wiring, a first response or a results exposure. A first response is never lost or changed by leaving, by a room change or by the results. A partial or review-closed series never shows results. A completed result never returns to `pending`. A reload never produces a fresh trial. A fault closes the series as a technical failure and leaves the laboratory usable.

**10 Scientific acceptance criteria — feature and extractor**

`m15_correct_first_predictions` (primary; the only M15 feature row): value = numerator = questions whose FIRST response is the keyed option; denominator = questions with a first response (option or cannot solve) in the current page load; planned denominator 4 (`planned_observations`). Cannot solve and a wrong option are in the denominator, not the numerator. A question without a first response — unpresented (its box's wiring not recorded, or the earlier question unanswered) or presented and unanswered — is missing and outside the denominator, never incorrect. The recorded wiring, its correctness, the tests run, help, drafts, time and input mode never change the numerator or the denominator; an answer counts whatever wiring was recorded and whatever tests were run.

Dispositions [O-5][D-6]:
- all four answered (`first_responses_completed`) ⇒ `observed`, `closure_reason: completed` (0 is an observed zero), stable whatever happens afterwards;
- one to three answered, series closed at the review ⇒ `incomplete` with the value and its denominator, censored, `closure_reason: closed_at_review`;
- never opened: before the briefing ⇒ `not_presented` (also at the review closure when never briefed); briefed, the opportunity open ⇒ null `pending` (`missing_reason` `briefed_not_opened`); briefed, at the review closure ⇒ null `no_eligible_event`, `briefed_not_opened`, censored, `closed_at_review` (the kit's `markAbsent` detail — a missing code, never a refusal); never `declined`;
- opened, nothing answered, closed at the review ⇒ null `no_eligible_event`, `missing_reason` `orientation_only` | `no_wiring_recorded` | `wiring_only_no_first_response` (as reached), censored, `closed_at_review`; still open ⇒ null `pending`;
- [O-8] one to three answered, still open ⇒ null `pending` with the answers so far in the components (`incomplete` only at the review closure);
- held back after a reload ⇒ null `interrupted` (also when the earlier load had completed all four); a reloaded load without its own opening ⇒ `interrupted` unless at least one `prior_load_checked` record exists in the load and every such record establishes the absence with its flags agreeing (established, continuous, no opening found, at least one earlier record) [O-6], in which case the load is read exactly as a first load; a first-response-phase technical failure ⇒ null `technical_failure`, the earlier answers kept in the components and never valued;
- precedence: `interrupted` > `technical_failure` > `pending` > the closed-series outcomes.

Extraction rules: current-load events only; pure and deterministic; the raw log byte-identical before and after. The value is RECOUNTED from the `first_response` events: each response's correctness is recomputed from `m15SystemsContent`'s key for that question and content version and compared with the event's `correct` flag and with the closure snapshot. `technical_failure` — never an observed value — for contradictory, malformed or unverifiable SCORED evidence only: an unknown or mismatched `entry_state_version`; an unknown `box_id`, `question_id` or `option_id`, or a `content_version` that does not match the box; two `first_response` events for one question; a `first_response` without that question's preceding `question_presented`; a `question_presented` before its box's `wiring_recorded`, before the previous question's `first_response`, out of the assigned order or twice; a `box_presented` out of order or twice; a `correct` flag that disagrees with the key; a cannot-solve marked correct or carrying a non-null `option_id`; an option response without an `option_id` or with another question's option; a non-boolean `correct`; a `first_response` outside phase `measurement` or after `first_responses_completed`; four responses without the completion snapshot, or the snapshot with fewer than four; a closure snapshot that disagrees with the recount; ANY `results_shown` not preceded by `first_responses_completed`; a `question_id` that does not belong to the event's `box_id`; an event `key_option_id` that disagrees with the content key; a family event of the current load without a usable `sequence` (a safe integer ≥ 1) or two sharing one (§5.259; gaps are normal); a `presented` or `prior_load_checked` record of another opportunity or version, or without a usable sequence, on either path (§5.284 / §5.290 (a) precedent). Legitimate missingness is never a technical failure. A defect confined to unscored records — a `test_run` after the box's `wiring_recorded`, two `wiring_recorded` for one box, a `wiring_recorded` whose `correct` disagrees with the wiring key, an orphan draft, a help record without a box — sets `model_record_consistent: false` or `exposure_record_consistent: false` in the components and never changes the row.

Components (companions beside the value, never inside it): **exposure stages, kept distinct** — `briefed` (a current-load `presented`) with its sequence, `bench_opened`, `orientation_acknowledged`, `boxes_presented`, `questions_presented`; administration and content versions; assigned and realised box and question order; `observations_share_one_episode: true`; `first_response_phase_complete`; **by box** — numerator, denominator and planned 2 for box 1 and box 2; **omissions** — `unanswered_question_ids` (presented without a first response) and `unpresented_question_ids`, by box, apart from cannot solve; **model** — per box the recorded wiring (option id | `cannot_tell` | none), `wiring_correct` (boolean | null when none), `models_correct` / `models_recorded` / planned 2; **exploration** — per box runs per dial before the wiring, `dials_tested_before_wiring`, `both_dials_tested_before_wiring`, total runs; **per question** — response kind, option, correctness, `consistent_with_recorded_wiring`, drafts before, help consults before, active time; `cannot_solve_count`, `cannot_tell_count`; help consults by phase; `exposure_record_consistent`; `model_record_consistent`; `reload_check`. No total that mixes model, exploration and prediction correctness; no total across items. `declined` never occurs for M15. The cipher's secondary events are never read.

Keys: the keys of the approved preview (D-U18-1 item 1); their derivation from the system definitions is verified by tests independent of the implementation (§12 P1).

**11 Gameplay acceptance criteria**

The ordinary route (Dock → … → Diagnostics Laboratory, Kai's briefing) reaches the evidence table without state injection; the bench is usable by keyboard alone and by pointer alone; every state has a way out (no soft lock; ESC order as §3.7); every confirmation states that the record cannot be changed; no record is made by a carried, held, repeated or doubled press, and no carried press acts in a newly opened view (§3.4.8); the header always shows the box and the step; the test record and the recorded wiring stay visible during the questions; nothing on screen or in sound differs with correctness before the fourth answer; the results make plain that the answers are fixed; text legible and unclipped in the wide frame (12 CSS px body text at 800 × 600) within the §3.8 envelope; no forbidden word. The wall display, beacon, Noor's lines, the other three benches, Kai's briefing and loan offer, the M10 / M11 behaviours of the laboratory and the route onward to the yard are unchanged.

Rules of evidence:
- Mockup evidence (`layout-evidence\`) and the preparation baseline (§12a) are reported separately from real-game verification; a mockup figure never stands in for a real-game result.
- A failure is never called pre-existing because of recorded history, this contract's §12a or a matching line number. A baseline-failure claim requires the SAME failure reproduced on an untouched export of exactly `f822eb46c174142a4c7566326dc0df077183bf19`: `git archive` of that commit into the session scratchpad, a `node_modules` junction to the primary, `PW_DEV_PORT=5202`, only the affected test (`--grep` its exact title, the base version of the spec), `--workers=1 --retries=0`; compare the failing assertion, its message and the step reached on both trees and keep both outputs. Same assertion, message and step ⇒ pre-existing; anything else ⇒ a U18 regression or unexplained. A base run that cannot reach the failing step proves nothing ("not comparable on the base"); a test that needs Git history (`final_scientific_gates.spec.ts:205`) cannot be compared on an export at all (§12a) and is reported as not comparable, never as pre-existing. No extra base worktree is created for a comparison. The export is never deleted recursively (it contains a junction).
- For every failure state whether it prevents verification of an M15 step; a failure before or at an M15 step leaves that step NOT VERIFIED by that run, even when pre-existing.
- One repeat may diagnose; a pass only on repetition is a flake and is reported as one. Never rerun until green. A suite that passed is not rerun unless a file it covers changed or a concern about it is open.
- Formatting complaints are compared by CONTENT, never by line number — format a scratch copy, diff it, separate lines this unit added or changed (fixed) from untouched base text (pre-existing only if the base file fails the same check; reported, not fixed). The matrix's and UNIT-LOG's inherited Prettier state at `f822eb4` is compared the same way.
- Not run, and reported as such: the capture specs, `world_v1_*`, `world_v2_lab_look` (registry and labels unchanged), `pilot_episodes_1_2` (Concourse untouched; its M05 step is the open §5.290 (e) (i) matter), and every spec not named above.
- While writing, Fable may run P1 and single `--grep` scenarios. The final S, P1, P2, B1, B2 matrix is run once by the Sonnet test-reviewer on the final source; after a correction only the affected checks are rerun. A command expected to exceed about nine minutes runs in the background and its completion notification is awaited — no polling, no log-watching loop.

**14 Stop conditions**

Stop the affected part, finish all independent authorised work, then report — never guess past: the gate line not `APPROVED` (a stop before the first edit); a genuine scientific conflict that would change the procedure, eligibility, exposure, key, denominator or formula of §3 / §10, or an instruction contradicting §2.1 or the ruling; a content defect in a key or a wiring option (a second defensible answer, an answer fixed without testing, a listing that the semantics do not produce) — the content is never re-authored by the implementer, the finding is recorded for the owner; correctness information reaching the participant before the fourth answer that cannot be removed inside the allowlist; a needed file outside the allowlist (in particular `windowKit.ts`, `WorkSurfaceScene.ts`, `pilotCoverage.ts`, `interactionRegistry.ts`, a helper); the §3.8 layout envelope not met in the real game (smaller text, scrolling or wrapping the wiring options in the narrow column are the owner's call); a guard rejection of a necessary action; a required reviewer model unavailable (never substitute Fable); an unexplained deterministic failure in the unit's own tests; a laboratory behaviour of another item that cannot be preserved; a material finding still open after the second review / fix round; entry state not matching §6. Missing git identity, a dirty or foreign worktree, or a wrong base is a stop before the first edit. In every stop case no completion is claimed, nothing is reset, stashed or discarded, and the handoff is resumable. Join every reviewer, test and shell; stop only dev servers this unit started.

**15 Model selection and review**

- Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`): the only writer — implementation, tests, docs, fixes.
- Sonnet 5.5 via `test-reviewer`: the named tests, the static checks and log analysis; edits nothing.
- Opus 5.5 via `scientific-reviewer` (measurement, keys and their derivation as implemented, unseen-ness, model / exploration kept apart from the value, the absence of correctness information before the fourth answer, the cipher's separation, events, extractor, register and addendum text, authority boundaries), `gameplay-reviewer` (flow, exploration and commitment controls, carried presses and transitions, keyboard and pointer use, recovery, wording, laboratory preservation) and `visual-reviewer` (screenshots 01–24): independent, read-only, in parallel on the final source after the Sonnet matrix; each cites file:line, a test or a screenshot.
- `cheap-explorer` (Haiku 4.5): narrowly bounded read-only lookups only.
- If a named agent is not discoverable, a general-purpose agent with the matching model override is used after it reads the role file, and this is reported. The actual model of every agent is recorded. No reviewer runs on Fable; an unavailable reviewer model is a stop condition.
- At most two review / fix rounds. Fixes are bounded: inside the allowlist, addressing cited, material findings. After a fix the affected checks are rerun (Sonnet) and the reviewer whose finding it answered confirms the material fix against the final source. Screenshots are regenerated only where a fix changed what they show. Reviewer findings are recommendations: a reviewer never approves a mapping, an event name, a formula, a key or a default and never reopens ruling D-U18-1; a finding needing an owner decision is recorded in register §5.

**16 Commit expectation and handoff**

Exactly one new local commit on `codex/u18-m15`, only after the verification of §12 and the review of §15 are complete, files staged one by one by explicit name, no amend, no hook bypass:

`feat(m15): add two relay boxes with immutable first predictions`

Untracked metadata that is not the unit's is never staged; if it makes `verify-unit` report an extra path, the exception is disclosed exactly and the guard, the verifier and ignore rules are never changed to hide it. If the gates are not met (correction rounds exhausted, a stop condition, a blocked essential check), there is NO commit: the working tree is left as it is and the handoff says so. Then the bounded-unit 12-field handoff, adding: the exact changed files against the allowlist, the commit hash (or "no commit" with the reason), every command with its true result, screenshot paths, the actual model and status of every agent, resolved and unresolved findings, ruling D-U18-1 as implemented with its date, the two boxes' content versions, wirings and keys by id, every default of §17 as implemented, the keyboard-navigation steps of the pointer scenario, process deviations, every failure with its base comparison (or "not compared") and whether it prevents verification of M15, every blocked or unrun check named, and the status of every background task (all joined). No "all checks passed" while any exception remains. Stop before U19; no push, merge, PR, tag, deployment or deletion.

**2.2 RESEARCH-OWNER DECISION D-U19-1 — APPROVED 11 October 2026 (with amendment A1)**

**The owner's ruling (11 October 2026), recorded against exactly this contract and preview r3:** items 1–9 are APPROVED as recommended below, including selection (a) of item 2 — the drawer confirmation repeats the drafted drawer; amendment A1 (end of this section) is APPROVED. The approval is for the provisional U19 / M16 implementation; it does not establish psychometric validity, questionnaire equivalence or that a correct answer shows understanding. The items are recorded as they were put to the owner — the proposal, the recommendation, the consequence and the alternatives considered — with the approved selection marked. Rules of this contract that implement an item are tagged [O-n]; rules that implement amendment A1 are tagged [A1-n]. Record the ruling and the amendment in the register (Unit 19 record and §5.302 onward) as an owner ruling with this date, not as implementer defaults; they are not to be reopened.

1. [O-1] Meaning of "two identical-structure teaching examples for everyone". Proposal: two PASSIVE worked examples (the rule applied step by step and explained; no answer requested; nothing recorded as a response), identical to each other in structure (the application label format, the same four numbered steps in the same order, one result line; each with exactly one mark present and one absent), shown identically, in the same order, to every participant, never contingent on performance (preview §1.1, §4). Recommendation: approve. Consequence: teaching gives no feedback on the participant's own answers; both examples end in DRAWER 3 (a consequence of the chosen coverage — both sites, both depth classes, each mark present and absent, one mark per example — preview §4); no worked example shows a no-mark or a two-mark vial. Alternatives: (a) two interactive practice items (the participant answers, then sees the worked explanation) — more active teaching; not inherently performance-dependent (every participant can be shown the same explanation whatever they answered), but it adds practice responses that need recording rules and must be kept out of the value, and the explanation then follows the participant's own answer, where it can be read as correctness feedback on that answer before the applications; (b) examples identical only to the application format, not to each other (e.g. one with no mark, one with both marks) — freer coverage, but not "identical in structure" to each other; (c) the same passive format with a pair that ends in different drawers, e.g. ORLA / 18 m / STAR (→ DRAWER 3) and VESK / 63 m / STAR, RING (→ DRAWER 1) — removes the DRAWER 3 attractor and shows the two-mark case, but never shows STAR absent and makes the two examples differ in their number of marks (an amendment: content and hashes change).
2. [O-2] Content. The rule, the two worked examples, the six vials, the four drawer options plus DON'T KNOW, the keys, every participant-facing string and the results explanations of preview r3 §3–§5 are the administered content (`m16-rule-v1`, `m16-examples-v1`, form `m16-form-1`); their logical correctness does not establish empirical validity. Recommendation: approve. Consequence: the keys are fixed — v1 `m16_v1_d1`, v2 `m16_v2_d3`, v3 `m16_v3_d4`, v4 `m16_v4_d1`, v5 `m16_v5_d4`, v6 `m16_v6_d2` (key sequence 1, 3, 4, 1, 4, 2; TOP / BOTTOM 3 / 3, ORLA / VESK column 3 / 3); blind-choice chance 1/4 per vial; the disclosed cues of preview §7 travel with the content (the no-mark vial v1 is answered correctly by 16 of the 23 listed non-guess strategies — every one that handles steps 1–2 as the rule does — passes through worked example 1 as an intermediate state, and comes first; the strongest listed strategies — swapped mark meanings and the absolute-direction readings STAR → TOP / BOTTOM row, RING → ORLA / VESK column — each give 4 of 6, so 4 of 6 does not separate slips from one consistent misreading; three of six vials need both marks; the rule card is visible throughout, so a ceiling is plausible). The set was re-selected in preview r2 after the preparation review found the absolute reading "STAR means TOP row" at 5 of 6 on the r1 set (preview §12). Within this item the drawer confirmation wording: (a) RECOMMENDED and SELECTED by the owner (11 October 2026) — `Record DRAWER <n> for vial N?` / `It cannot be changed afterwards.` (repeats the drafted drawer, so a slip can be caught before recording; the drafted drawer is already highlighted on screen, so this adds no new information); or (b) `Record this answer for vial N?` / `It cannot be changed afterwards.` (the M15 wording; no repetition) — not selected. Alternative to the whole item: ask the preparation to revise the content (other qualifying sets of `derivation/search-sets.out.json`, a harder rule, or a different number of options) — the unit then waits.
3. [O-3] Information available while answering ("instructions available"). Proposal: the complete rule card stays on screen beside every vial; the worked examples close at the boundary and are never shown again; earlier vials' labels and answers are not shown; HELP explains controls only. Recommendation: approve. Consequence: the measure concerns applying a visible rule to unseen labels, not recall; a ceiling is plausible; no "consulted the instructions" companion exists because the instructions are never hidden. Alternatives: (a) the rule card on request only (a REFERENCE control, consults recorded as a companion) — adds a memory demand and a use-of-instructions record, but "instructions available" then depends on the participant's choice to consult; (b) the worked examples re-viewable during the vials on request (recorded) — more support, but teaching exposure then varies between participants after the boundary.
4. [O-4] Teaching pace, repetition and the boundary. Proposal: self-paced reading; free movement between example 1 and example 2 (NEXT EXAMPLE / BACK TO EXAMPLE 1) any number of times before the boundary; no minimum reading time, no comprehension check, no practice vial; the boundary is START THE SIX VIALS with a confirmation (preview §3.4) — confirming closes teaching irreversibly and presents vial 1; leaving during teaching keeps the example in view and reopening returns to it. Recommendation: approve. Consequence: teaching time and example views vary between participants and are recorded as companions only; nothing in teaching enters the value. Alternatives: a minimum display time per example; a single forced pass (no BACK); a comprehension check before the vials (adds an unscored response and an eligibility question).
5. [O-5] Feedback timing and results. Proposal: an identical neutral acknowledgement after every first response (`Vial N recorded.`, `N of 6 vials recorded.`, NEXT VIAL / SHOW RESULTS) — no colour, glyph, sound, wording, layout or timing that differs with correctness; no correctness information about any vial until all six first responses are recorded; then two results views (vials 1–3, 4–6) with the recorded drawer (or DON'T KNOW), the rule's drawer and the two-line explanation of preview §5 (their controls as amended by A1-2); results re-viewable read-only on reopening; a partial or review-closed series never shows results. Recommendation: approve. Consequence: the results cannot inform any first response. Alternative: no results at all (no corrective feedback — contradicts the summary's "corrective feedback only after all six first responses"), or a tally line (adds a performance count the other items avoid).
6. [O-6] Order and form. Proposal: one form, fixed vial order v1 → v6, fixed option order DRAWER 1–4, no counterbalancing; the legacy counterbalanced forms A / B are not used on the route; the "form, example versions" companions are recorded as `form_id` `m16-form-1`, `rule_version` `m16-rule-v1`, `examples_version` `m16-examples-v1` (constant in this administration). Recommendation: approve (M14 / M15 used one form; D-U17-1 item 3 and D-U18-1 item 7 are precedent only). Consequence: vial content and position are confounded; the likely easiest vial (v1) comes first. Alternative: two forms with assignment and order counterbalancing (a second authored form, assignment logic, and an order-effect analysis at a small n).
7. [O-7] Briefing exposure and voluntary non-use (the M14 / M15 convention — precedent only; approved for M16 by this ruling). Proposal: Kai's laboratory briefing, which names the protocol console, records the M16 briefing exposure at its acknowledgement (the kit's `present`, in all four `lab_brief_ack*` handlers) — exposure only. Before the briefing `not_presented`; briefed, never opened, open ⇒ null `pending` (`briefed_not_opened`); briefed, never opened, at the review closure ⇒ null `no_eligible_event`, `briefed_not_opened`, censored, `closed_at_review`; `declined` never occurs; there is no STOP control — leaving is the only exit and never records DON'T KNOW. Recommendation: approve. Alternative: the general dispositions without the briefing distinction; or a STOP control coded as voluntary stop (adds a refusal path the approved row does not ask for).
8. [O-8] Reload (the §5.290 (a) / D-U18-1 item 6 convention — precedent only; approved for M16 by this ruling). Proposal: an opening of this administration in an earlier page load of the session identity ⇒ the console is never re-run in the new load (neutral closed record of preview §3.10; prior exposure recorded; the load's row `interrupted`; the earlier events immutable); at the first Diagnostics Laboratory entry of a later page load the adapter writes `prior_load_checked` (the §5.290 (a) fields); an established absence of an earlier opening with continuous history reads the load exactly as a first load. Recommendation: approve. Consequence: a never-opened console after a reload is not misread as interrupted; one more record and its integrity rules; prior exposure stays uncertain where the history is discontinuous (§3.7). Alternative: the general rule only — every reloaded load without M16 evidence is `interrupted`.
9. [O-9] Partial evidence while the opportunity is open (the D-U18-1 item 8 convention — precedent only; approved for M16 by this ruling). Proposal: one to five first responses and the series not yet closed ⇒ null `pending` with the recorded answers in the components; at the review closure ⇒ `incomplete` with the value and its observed denominator. A session ending before the review exports `pending`. Recommendation: approve. Alternative: export `incomplete` with the value whenever at least one answer exists, also while the series is open (a value that can still change in a later export of the same session).

**AMENDMENT A1 — APPROVED 11 October 2026 (research owner).** Four corrections to the package; none changes the rule, the worked examples, the six labels, the keys, the order, the scoring, the missingness or the reload policies.
- [A1-1] Accurate recording language. No participant string or contract statement claims that nothing is recorded where views, navigation, drafts or help use are logged. Teaching says `No answer is requested on this page.`; the help says `Only confirming records your answer.` and `... then RECORD DRAWER and confirm, or DON'T KNOW and confirm.`; the reload record says `... Its record is kept; no further answers can be given here.`; an ANSWER (a `first_response`) is always distinguished from a LOGGED INTERACTION (a view, navigation, draft, help consult or refused request). Closed-record statements that accurately promise no further family events are kept (§3.7, R3).
- [A1-2] Complete, consistent controls. Results page 1: HELP, FINISH and NEXT; results page 2: HELP, FINISH and BACK (preview §3.9 positions; NEXT and BACK never share a position). Acknowledgements: HELP and LEAVE CONSOLE beside NEXT VIAL / SHOW RESULTS. FINISH and ESC close the results surface. Completion is established by the sixth first response whatever results pages are later viewed; `results_shown` is written only for a page actually displayed, once per page. HELP / CLOSE HELP return to the same page with all state preserved. The 400 ms transition protection covers every results transition, so no carried press navigates, closes, duplicates an exposure record or changes a response. Reopening stays read-only. The results controls are verified through actual pointer and keyboard interaction (§12 R1, R2, R9).
- [A1-3] Unambiguous double-click verification. The opener `RECORD DRAWER  [R]` (vial view, right column) and the dialog's confirm `RECORD DRAWER  [ENTER]` (dialog, panel (200, 250)) are distinct controls. A double click on the opener records ZERO first responses (the dialog opens; the second click lands on no control or inside the dialog's 400 ms fresh-press window and is refused). A fresh confirm after the protection interval records EXACTLY ONE first response, and a duplicate press immediately after it changes nothing. The existing protections against held keys, auto-repeat and carried presses stay (§3.4).
- [A1-4] Consistent approval and package status: D-U19-1 recorded as APPROVED 11 October 2026 with A1 in this contract, the preview (r3), the launch prompt and the launcher; documentation overstatements corrected (preview §1.1, §6, §7, §12; item 1 alternative (a) and item 2 above). Integrity pins regenerated.

Ordinary engineering (not decision items; recorded as defaults in §17): the commitment mechanics (fresh press, settle), focus landings, the leaving rules of §3.7, the layout positions inside the §3.9 envelope, the event and identifier names of §9, the extractor's integrity rules, and the disposition of the legacy module (§3.1).

**2.3 Claims this unit never makes**

The six applications are repeated observations of ONE rule inside ONE console episode — not six independent situations; the vials are not equated in difficulty; the content is one authored form; a correct answer is never proof of understanding; teaching time, example views, help, drafts and response time are companions, never part of the value; passing tests establishes implementation correctness, never psychometric validity or questionnaire equivalence. No global or cross-item score. Participant-facing text never contains the criterion stem or its words (preview §9). The v2 protocol-update task, its forms and the frozen v2 ledger are historical. Never fall back to the legacy terminal task on the route.

**3 Participant-facing behaviour — administration `m16-handling-v1`**

Each rule is tagged [A] approved row or owner instruction, [O-n] decision D-U19-1 item n (APPROVED 11 October 2026), [A1-n] amendment A1 part n, [P] precedent, or [D-n] implementer default listed in §17. Ordinary engineering details inside the envelope are the implementer's and are recorded.

**3.1 Place, access and the legacy module**
- [A] The Diagnostics Laboratory protocol console (phase 2 of the signal case; registry id `lab.phase_m16`, its label "Protocol Console" and approach unchanged), opened as the generic `WorkSurfaceScene` in the WIDE frame of decision D-U17-2, unchanged, with surface id `m16_protocol_console`; bench label "Protocol Console", phase name "Handling protocol", operational label "Signal case — protocol (Laboratory)", episode 3.
- [O-7][P] Optional, as today: enterable whenever no other phase surface is open; Kai's dialogue text unchanged; no gate, reward, judgement or route consequence. Every one of the FOUR `onSelected` handlers of Kai's briefing acknowledgement (`lab_brief_ack` in the no-loan-offer branch; `lab_brief_ack`, `lab_brief_ack_loan_accept`, `lab_brief_ack_loan_decline` in the loan-offer branch; base `DiagnosticsLaboratoryScene.ts` ≈ lines 1008–1071, each already calling `advancePilotStage('lab_work', now)` and `presentM15(now)`) also calls `presentM16(now)`; P1 asserts by source that each of the four does. The stage at the first opening is recorded in the entry snapshot.
- [P] The phase order, the beacon, the wall display (its "Protocol lanes" ticks once M16 is recorded), Noor's line `NOOR · relay: The handling protocol is on the console.` and the case brief are unchanged; the display's "recorded" state follows the M16 window's closure (completed or closed).
- [D-10] The legacy module `src/informationProcessing/m16ProtocolUpdate.ts` (and `protocolForms.ts`) stays in the tree UNCHANGED, keeps its frozen v2 identity (`proto_m16_protocol_update`, `proto_m16_protocol_*`, `m16_protocol_w1`, entry `m16-protocol-v1`) and stays reachable only through the developer alias `?scene=information_processing_lab` (`InformationProcessingLabScene.ts`, unchanged). The laboratory scene no longer imports it. The v3 extractor never reads its family (`proto_m16_handling_` and `proto_m16_protocol_` are disjoint prefixes). The interaction registry's descriptive `opens: { kind: 'ip_overlay', id: 'm16' }` and window label `m16_protocol_update` for `lab.phase_m16` are NOT changed (out of the allowlist; U24 backlog, as U18 left `m15_layered_cipher`); the scene's own station construction decides what opens.

**3.2 Content, order and form**
- [O-2][A1-1] Content exactly as preview r3 §3–§5 (first-opening card, rule card, worked examples, boundary confirmation, vial views, options, keys, confirmations, acknowledgements, help, results, closed records). Line breaks are those of the preview (fixed); wording, letters, numbers, order and option order never change. The participant strings live in one pure content module; no questionnaire wording anywhere.
- [O-6] One form, fixed vial order v1 → v6, fixed option order DRAWER 1–4; realised order always equals assigned order.
- [O-3] Objective access while answering: the rule card, the current vial's label, the four options, the status line, HELP. The worked examples are never rendered after the boundary.

**3.3 First opening and teaching**
1. [D-2] The first opening shows the first-opening card (preview §3.1) with SHOW EXAMPLE 1; activating it is recorded (`intro_acknowledged`); leaving before it shows the card again at the next opening.
2. [O-1][O-4] Example 1, then example 2 (preview §3.3, §4); NEXT EXAMPLE and BACK TO EXAMPLE 1 move between them any number of times; every view is logged (`example_viewed`, with the example and its view index) as an interaction, never as an answer; nothing in teaching is a response [A1-1].
3. [O-4] START THE SIX VIALS (example 2 only) opens the boundary confirmation (preview §3.4); a fresh confirming press records `teaching_closed` once (examples viewed, back-navigations, teaching active time, help consults before) and presents vial 1; KEEP READING / ESC returns to example 2 and records `teaching_close_cancelled`. After `teaching_closed` no view renders an example.

**3.4 A vial**
1. Vial view (preview §3.5): left the rule card and the vial label; right the question, four option tiles, the opener `RECORD DRAWER  [R]`, `DON'T KNOW  [N]`; bottom row HELP and LEAVE CONSOLE. Activating a tile (pointer, ENTER / SPACE on focus, or 1–4) makes it the draft, another replaces it, the same again clears it; drafts are logged (`option_drafted`) as interactions, never as a response, and survive leaving and returning [D-3][A1-1]. Only confirming records an answer.
2. [O-2][A1-3] Commitment: the opener `RECORD DRAWER  [R]` with a draft opens the drawer confirmation, which repeats the drafted drawer (item 2 selection (a)); `DON'T KNOW` opens its confirmation whatever the draft; without a draft the opener shows `Choose a drawer first.` and logs `commit_without_draft` only (no answer). Only the dialog's confirm control `RECORD DRAWER  [ENTER]` (or `RECORD  [ENTER]` for DON'T KNOW) records an answer. [P][D-4] Only a fresh confirming press commits — a press inside the first 400 ms after the dialog appeared, the press that opened it, a held key or an auto-repeat never confirms; a held key or auto-repeat is dropped by the surface before the host (`WorkSurfaceScene.ts` `guardKeyHandler`, `event.repeat`) and is never recorded; `commit_press_refused` records the non-fresh presses that reach the host; a doubled confirmation records one response (M02 §5.210, M13 §5.262, M14, M15 precedent). [A1-3] Consequently: a double click on the OPENER records zero first responses (the dialog opens with its 400 ms fresh-press window; the second click lands on no control or is refused and logged as `commit_press_refused`); a fresh press of the dialog's CONFIRM after the 400 ms interval records exactly one `first_response`, and a duplicate press immediately after it lands on the acknowledgement view inside its settle and changes nothing. The confirm control is never at the screen position of the control that opened the dialog (dialog controls at panel (200, 250) / (466, 250), every opener at x ≥ 738 or in the bottom row). While a dialog or the help sheet is open the model renders only the header, the status line and that dialog or sheet; the confirm (or CLOSE HELP) control is the first focusable element; 1–4 / R / N do nothing. KEEP WORKING / ESC closes the dialog without a response (`commit_cancelled`).
3. [A] DON'T KNOW: an incorrect first response whatever the draft; visually and textually distinct from LEAVE CONSOLE and never adjacent to it; leaving never records DON'T KNOW.
4. [A] A first response is written once (`first_response`) and is immutable: no later act, reopening, results view, reload or closure changes or duplicates it.
5. [O-5][A1-2] Identical neutral acknowledgement for every response whatever its kind or correctness (preview §3.7), with `HELP  [H]` and `LEAVE CONSOLE` in the bottom row beside the primary NEXT VIAL / SHOW RESULTS. The next vial is presented only from the acknowledgement (NEXT VIAL), so each vial's presentation follows the previous vial's first response.
6. [P][D-4] Settle on EVERY view transition: a press arriving within 400 ms after a view appeared — the first-opening card's SHOW EXAMPLE 1, an example view, the boundary confirmation's restored example 2, a vial's first view, an acknowledgement, each results page (its NEXT / BACK / FINISH / HELP), the help sheet and the view restored by CLOSE HELP — changes nothing (no draft, navigation, close, commit request, help consult or `results_shown`) [A1-2]. CLOSE HELP and a cancelled dialog re-arm the restored view's settle. No carried press — the second ENTER, the second click of a double click, a repeated key — drafts, requests, confirms, navigates or closes in a newly opened view.

**3.5 Results [O-5][A1-2]**
Only when all six first responses are recorded. SHOW RESULTS opens page 1 (vials 1–3) with HELP, FINISH and NEXT; NEXT opens page 2 (vials 4–6) with HELP, FINISH and BACK; BACK returns to page 1 (positions: preview §3.9, §10 — NEXT and BACK never share a position). FINISH and ESC close the results surface from either page. Completion is established by the sixth first response (`first_responses_completed`), whichever results pages are later viewed; FINISH from page 1 is legitimate and leaves page 2 unrecorded. `results_shown` (with its page) is written only when a page is actually displayed, and only at its first display. HELP opens the help sheet; CLOSE HELP returns to the same page with all state preserved and re-arms its settle. No results act changes a response. Reopening a completed console shows page 1 again, read-only; a page first displayed on a reopening is recorded then, once.

**3.6 Help [D-5]**
HELP (H or the button) on the first-opening card, both examples, every vial view, every acknowledgement and both results pages — never while a dialog is open; the preview §3.8 sheet; informational; every consult logged (`help_consulted`) with the phase and the view or results page it was opened on — an interaction, never an answer. CLOSE HELP (H or the button) returns to the same view with all state (example, vial, draft, results page) preserved and re-arms its settle [A1-2].

**3.7 Leaving, closure, reload, faults**
- [P] ESC closes, in order, an open dialog, then the help sheet, then leaves; LEAVE CONSOLE leaves; both take the SAME path (window pause, clock pause, surface close — the `m15SurfaceHost` / `m14SurfaceHost` precedent). Leaving keeps everything (phase, example view, vial, draft, answers); returning never presents a vial again and never starts a new trial; leaving in a dialog cancels the dialog and records no response. There is no STOP control.
- HELP and LEAVE CONSOLE are reachable through actual controls by pointer and by keyboard on every view where the preview lists them (first-opening card, both examples, every vial view with or without a draft, every acknowledgement) and HELP and FINISH on both results pages (the results pages have no LEAVE CONSOLE; FINISH or ESC closes them) — verified in the browser through the actual controls by pointer and by keyboard (§12 B1 R1, R2, R9) [A1-2].
- [P] Station-record closure at the Utility Deck review (`reviewClosure.ts` → `closeM16AtReview`, after `closeM15AtReview`): a series opened and not complete (first-opening card, teaching, or 0–5 vials answered) closes as `closed_at_review` (system): recorded answers kept, unanswered vials missing; no results afterwards; the console then opens as the closed record of preview §3.10 showing `N of 6 vials recorded.`; while a closed record (review or reload) is shown no answer can be given and no `proto_m16_handling_` event is written [A1-1]. A completed series is not reclosed. A never-opened console is recorded absent with the kit's `markAbsent` (`briefed_not_opened` / `not_briefed_not_opened`).
- [O-8][P] Reload: an opening of this administration in an earlier page load ⇒ the hold-back (closed record, prior exposure recorded, the series marked technically incomplete, the earlier events immutable in `prior_page_load_events`) — also when the earlier load completed all six. `prior_load_checked` once per later page load at the first `guardM16Reload` run (Diagnostics Laboratory `create()`), before the hold-back record when an opening is found. A console never opened before the reload runs normally. Limitations carried unchanged from §5.290 (a): the check is made only where the console becomes available (a reloaded load that never reaches the laboratory keeps `interrupted`); continuity is read from recovered sequence numbers and the store's meta record and cannot reveal a lost tail when the meta record survived — prior exposure after a reload is therefore uncertain, never proven absent; after a reload Kai's briefing replays and the earlier briefing is reported in the check, never counted as this load's exposure.
- A fault while the series is open closes it as a technical failure through the window kit and leaves the laboratory usable; a dialog never stays stuck after a cancelled callback.

**3.8 Lifecycle states (explicit)**
| State | Defined by | Row (§10) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| not presented | no current-load `presented`, no opening | `not_presented` |
| briefed, never opened (open) | `presented`, no `opportunity_opened` | null `pending`, `briefed_not_opened` |
| open — card / teaching / 0 answers | opened, no `first_response` | null `pending` |
| open — 1–5 answers | 1–5 `first_response`, no closure | null `pending`, answers in components [O-9] |
| complete | `first_responses_completed` (six answers) | `observed`, `completed`, stable |
| incomplete | closed at the review with 1–5 answers | `incomplete`, value on the observed denominator, censored |
| closed with no answer | closed at the review with 0 answers | null `no_eligible_event`, `missing_reason` `intro_only` / `teaching_only` / `teaching_closed_no_first_response` |
| briefed, never opened, closed | `markAbsent` at the review | null `no_eligible_event`, `briefed_not_opened`, censored |
| interrupted | hold-back after a reload, or a reloaded load without an established absence | null `interrupted` |
| technically invalid | fault while open, or contradictory / malformed scored evidence | null `technical_failure` |

**3.9 Wording and presentation limits**
Forbidden in every participant-facing string of the console (tested by pattern, case-insensitive): `proto_`, `secondary_`, `M##`, `Q##`, score, trait, puzzle, persist, grit, skill, ability, intelligen, information, process, learn, quick, the word "new", and the Console Orientation terms ROUTE, fragment, destination, ARCHIVE, RELAY, ALPHA, BETA, codebook, channel, program, buffer, SUBMIT. Before the sixth first response no correctness word (correct, incorrect, right, wrong, "rule's drawer"). No praise, blame or judgement (review criterion). [A1-1] No string claims that nothing is recorded where views, navigation, drafts or help are logged; teaching says "No answer is requested on this page." and the help "Only confirming records your answer."; an answer is never conflated with a logged interaction. Pointer and keyboard each reach every control. Layout envelope (mockup evidence `layout-evidence\`): 16 px design text, 20 px title; the rule card and the vial label in the 714 px left column; the four drawer tiles, the opener RECORD DRAWER and DON'T KNOW in the 300 px right column; the results controls HELP, FINISH and NEXT / BACK in the bottom row at the preview §10 positions; results explanations on fixed lines; one-line footer; at least 30 design px between the lowest control and the feedback line's top under the default font and under forced Courier New and Lucida Console; never smaller text, clipped or re-wrapped wording, scrolling, or a larger minimum window.

**7 Success behaviour**

On the ordinary route (routeToLabWork, Kai's briefing) the protocol console presents the first-opening card, the rule with both worked examples (free movement between them), the confirmed boundary, then the six vials in order; each vial takes exactly one immutable first response — a confirmed drawer or a confirmed DON'T KNOW — answered only by the identical neutral acknowledgement; no correctness information appears before the sixth; then the results follow without touching any response; leaving and returning resume the same state; the export carries `m16_correct_first_applications` with value = numerator = vials whose first response is the keyed drawer, denominator = vials with a first response, planned denominator 6, the versions, per-vial records, omissions and teaching exposure in the components, and the dispositions of §10 — complete and stable from the sixth first response — reproducible from the raw events alone; the legacy module writes nothing on the route; every check of §12 was run and reported with its true result; the reviews of §15 are closed; one local commit exists (§16).

**8 Failure and recovery behaviour**

Never opened (before / after the briefing), opened at the card only, opened in teaching, teaching closed with no answer, one to five answers, closed at the review with or without answers, held back after a reload, technically failed and completed are distinct records (§3.8, §10). A double press, a doubled confirmation, a carried press into a new view, a re-entry or a resumed surface never duplicates a presentation, a `teaching_closed`, a first response or a results exposure. A first response is never lost or changed by leaving, a room change or the results. A partial or review-closed series never shows results. A completed result never returns to `pending`. A reload never produces a fresh trial. A fault closes the series as a technical failure and leaves the laboratory usable.

Family `proto_m16_handling_`; ONE opportunity `proto_m16_handling_series`; window `m16_handling_w1`; object `m16_protocol_console`; `entry_state_version` `m16-handling-v1`; `form_id` `m16-form-1`; `rule_version` `m16-rule-v1`; `examples_version` `m16-examples-v1`.
